Bash(gh pr create --title "feat: Add type-safe enum support to Stasis" --body "$(cat <<''EOF''
## Summary
Implements fully type-safe enums with compile-time guarantees that prevent mixing enum types with integers or other enum types.

## Features
- ✅ Enum declarations with sequential values starting from 0
- ✅ Member access via `EnumName.MemberName` syntax
- ✅ Strong type checking prevents invalid assignments
- ✅ Compile-time errors for type mismatches
- ✅ LLVM IR generation lowers enums to i32 constants

## Type Safety Guarantees
- 🔒 Enum variables must use enum type (not i32)
- 🔒 Cannot assign integers to enum variables
- 🔒 Cannot compare enums with integers
- 🔒 Cannot mix different enum types
- 🔒 Only same-type enum members can be assigned/compared

## Example Usage
```stasis
enum State { Idle, Jump, Run }

function update(): void {
    let state: State = State.Idle;  // ✓ Valid
    state = State.Jump;              // ✓ Valid
    
    if (state == State.Idle) {       // ✓ Valid
        state = State.Run;
    }
    
    // let x: State = 0;             // ✗ Error: cannot assign i32 to State
    // if (state == 0) {}            // ✗ Error: cannot compare State with i32
}
```

## Implementation
- **Parser**: Enum parsing already existed, enhanced member tracking
- **Semantic**: Added type resolution and compatibility checking for enums
- **IR**: Lower enum members to compile-time i32 constants
- **Tests**: 15 new tests covering parsing, semantics, and type safety
- **Sample**: Added `samples/test_enums.stasis` with runtime tests

## Test Results
- ✅ All 100 compiler tests pass
- ✅ All 3 enum runtime tests pass
- ✅ Type safety verified with error detection tests

## Documentation
- Updated `docs/spec.md` with comprehensive enum specification
- Added type safety rules and examples

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
